items.item_text: Licensed with the California Board of Behavioral Sciences
A valid mental health license in the state of California (Licensed Psychologist, LCSW, LMFT, LPCC)
5150 Certification for Alameda County within 30 days of employment
Master's or doctorate in a mental health field (psychology, counseling, social work, or a related field) and/or equivalent experience/training.

Minimum one year of experience providing behavioral health services in a public health, community mental health, crisis services, or other setting serving adults exhibiting mental health crisis, psychosis, substance-related mental health needs, etc.
Minimum one year of experience working with college/university students or young adults.
Demonstrated experience conducting behavioral health assessments and providing crisis intervention, de-escalation, and brief behavioral health interventions.
Demonstrated experience assessing behavioral health risk, including suicidality, homicidal intent, violence risk, grave disability, and/or substance-related concerns.
Demonstrated experience coordinating behavioral health care, referrals, and/or linkage to appropriate clinical, hospital, or community resources.
Experience documenting behavioral health assessments, interventions, and client responses in an electronic health record or comparable clinical documentation system.
Demonstrated experience collaborating with multidisciplinary teams and/or community partners in the coordination of behavioral health care.
Demonstrated experience providing culturally responsive services to individuals from a wide range of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives.

The Behavioral Health Counselor 3 serves as a member of the Ally Care Team (ACT), which is comprised of behavioral health clinicians and support staff. This position provides behavioral health consultations, care navigation, and episodic therapy to students, staff, and faculty on campus. The Behavioral Health Counselor 3 is responsible for providing these services within an integrated medical, mental health, and campus model. Duties include brief therapy, medical and staff consultations, care navigation support, de-escalation, intervention and assessment (including 5150 evaluation), support with non-critical welfare checks, and postvention support.

Must be able/willing to work flexibly and outside of a traditional clinical space, such as being outside during most of the shift, traveling in a vehicle and/or walking with others between crises, and physically move frequently during a shift.
